title: Signal · Sunday 8 November
overview: The UBS capital fight turns to a compromise idea, banks put numbers on AI, Binance traces its theft to a tampered AI tool, rates rise as AI stocks fall, and supervisors start inspecting bank AI.

top.headline: UBS capital fight turns to a compromise idea as FINMA's new powers draw fire
top.summary: A member of the National Council has proposed that UBS value its foreign subsidiaries under the equity method, which could reduce its future capital needs, Bloomberg reported on 4 November, according to cash.ch. How much is unclear, and support is far from certain. The Council of States voted in September for 90 percent CET1 backing of foreign units, about USD 16 billion of extra capital, against full backing in the Federal Council's bill.
top.background: The FINMA half of the package drew unusual fire: Oliver Buschan, director of the Association of Swiss Cantonal Banks, said the draft reads largely like a FINMA wish list and warned of a 'mega authority' (translated from German), according to finews; FINMA disputes this. UBS is also cutting about 200 London jobs as the Credit Suisse integration nears its end, Bloomberg reported.
top.why: The outcome sets UBS's capital and returns, and the FINMA powers set compliance costs for mid-sized Swiss banks.
top.watch_next: The National Council's economic affairs committee holds its detailed debate on 23 and 24 November.

top.headline: Banks put numbers on AI: UBS counts 608 use cases, Santander EUR 194 million
top.summary: UBS has 608 AI use cases in production, 81 percent more than a year earlier, with more than 1,090 in development, and staff run more than 12,700 personal AI agents, according to its third-quarter report as summarised by Fintech News Switzerland. Santander put AI's business value at EUR 194 million for the first nine months, according to Startup Fortune, and Intesa Sanpaolo listed 33 AI, generative and agentic AI initiatives with its results on 3 November.
top.background: Goldman Sachs moved the other way on tools, limiting AI coding tools including Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub to engineers and barring most traders and bankers, according to Bloomberg as reported by Quartz.
top.why: Counting use cases and euros moves AI in banks from pilots to the budget line, and boards elsewhere will ask for the same figures.

top.headline: Binance ties its USD 6.3 billion theft to a tampered AI coding tool
top.summary: Binance said on 3 November that the attack began in June, when a wallet developer downloaded a tampered AI coding tool, and that a second engineer later installed a malicious code repository after a fake job interview, NBC News reported. An internal AI tool then helped the attackers take control of its wallets before USD 6.3 billion was drained on 29 October. Chainalysis said attackers used 'offensive agentic techniques' to reach its systems, according to SecurityWeek.
top.background: On defence, OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber on 5 November to a small number of approved security customers, Fortune reported, and OpenAI president Greg Brockman disclosed a partnership with JPMorgan Chase covering its Codex coding agent and specialised cyber models, according to Crypto Briefing.
top.why: Developer machines and AI coding tools are now a route to client money, so banks rolling out coding agents need to control them like privileged access.

top.headline: Bank of England raises rates as AI stocks slide after the US midterms
top.summary: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4 percent on 5 November, its first rise since 2023, with eight committee members voting for a quarter point and one for half a point. On fears that Democrats' midterm gains could slow the AI buildout, the Nasdaq fell 5.52 percent on 5 November and closed in correction, in a sell-off that CNN put at about USD 2.5 trillion; Nvidia fell 9.3 percent.
top.background: Swiss inflation rose to 1.5 percent in October, its highest since December 2023, on petroleum products 40 percent dearer than a year earlier, SRF reported, while core inflation held at 0.5 percent. Bundesbank president Joachim Nagel said a December ECB rise is very likely necessary, according to Reuters as carried by Euronext.
top.why: Higher European rates help bank margins but raise funding and credit costs, and a correction in AI stocks puts AI budgets and valuations under closer scrutiny.
top.watch_next: The SNB decides on 10 December, the ECB and the Bank of England on 17 December.

top.headline: Supervisors start inspecting bank AI as FINMA unveils its own pilot
top.summary: The US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued a supervisory framework on 4 November telling examiners to classify banks' use of what it calls super intelligence by potential consequences, transfer of agency and human oversight rather than technical sophistication. The UK FCA's review of wholesale banks, published on 2 November, lists insufficient human oversight, unapproved tools leaking data, inadequate kill switches and incomplete AI inventories, according to Regulation Tomorrow.
top.background: FINMA chair Marlene Amstad presented Subsuma, FINMA's AI pilot for licensing questions, at the Swiss Bankers Association's Digital Finance Day on 3 November, and told institutions the question is no longer whether they use AI but whether they are in control of it.
top.why: Kill switches, inventories and named accountability are becoming examination items, so banks will need evidence of control as well as a policy.

items.headline: Safirum launches CHF-S, a whitelisted Swiss franc stablecoin on Solana
items.summary: Zug-based Safirum launched CHF-S on Solana on 3 November, backed one to one by accounts at Berner Kantonalbank and Banque Richelieu, according to finews. Only identified, whitelisted wallets can hold it and only institutional investors can mint it.
items.why: A first test of whether a franc token built within FINMA's stablecoin guidance can win institutional users, and a reference point for banks weighing their own.

items.headline: Zurich city pension fund halts its software migration after a vendor data theft
items.summary: The board of Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich suspended the new administration system planned for early 2027 and will keep its current one through 2027, finews reported on 3 November. Test data it had sent to the vendor, PK Softech, was among what criminals took in a late-September attack.
items.why: A vendor breach can stop a core migration outright, which belongs in every bank's and insurer's third-party risk plan.

items.headline: Claude adds Personal Finance, reading US bank accounts through Plaid
items.summary: Anthropic said on 5 November that Personal Finance is rolling out in beta on its Pro, Max and Ultra plans in the US. Users sign in to their bank through Plaid and can ask about balances, spending, fees and interest, with read-only access.
items.why: Puts an AI lab between customers and their bank data in the US, a channel banks will watch as open finance widens in Europe.

items.headline: Capgemini: 59 percent of financial firms try multi-agent AI, few at scale
items.summary: The Capgemini Research Institute's World Cloud Report for Financial Services 2027, published on 5 November and based on 1,100 executives, finds 59 percent of firms piloting or deploying multi-agent AI and 10 percent orchestrating it enterprise-wide.
items.why: The gap between pilots and enterprise-wide orchestration is where architecture, data and operating model work for banks sits.

items.headline: HSBC plans a Hong Kong AI institute and trains its whole workforce
items.summary: HSBC chief executive Georges Elhedery said on 2 November that the bank aims to open an AI and emerging technology institute in Hong Kong in the first quarter of 2027, with HKUST as anchor academic partner. AI training is being rolled out to its roughly 200,000 staff, according to AsiaOne.
items.why: Sets a benchmark for AI skills programmes that European and Swiss banks will be compared against.

items.headline: Valiant lifts nine-month profit 5.4 percent to CHF 114.2 million
items.summary: Valiant reported group profit up 5.4 percent to CHF 114.2 million for the first nine months on 5 November, helped by commission growth, according to finews.
items.why: A steady regional bank result, and a benchmark for Swiss retail banks as the rate outlook turns.

items.headline: Swiss Re earns USD 4.2 billion in nine months as reinsurance competition grows
items.summary: Swiss Re said on 5 November that nine-month net profit reached USD 4.2 billion, with a return on equity of 22.5 percent, and that it targets USD 4.5 billion for the year. Net profit in property and casualty reinsurance fell 6 percent in a more competitive market, according to finews.
items.why: Softer reinsurance pricing feeds into primary insurers' costs and into Swiss insurers' plans for 2027.

items.headline: Swiss franc bond issuance reaches CHF 89 billion, level with the 2009 record
items.summary: Bonds with a nominal value of CHF 89 billion reached the Swiss primary market by the end of October, level with the CHF 88.9 billion of 2009, finews reported on 4 November, citing Zürcher Kantonalbank statistics.
items.why: Busy capital markets support Swiss banks' underwriting and trading income in a year of thin lending margins.

items.headline: Commerzbank posts record nine-month operating profit of EUR 4 billion
items.summary: Commerzbank said on 5 November that operating profit rose 17.3 percent to EUR 4.037 billion and net profit 41.4 percent to EUR 2.669 billion, keeping its target of at least EUR 3.4 billion. Completion of UniCredit's offer still needs further clearances.
items.why: Record profits strengthen Commerzbank's position while UniCredit's takeover works through approvals.

items.headline: Lloyds opens voluntary redundancy as UK banks cut jobs
items.summary: Lloyds has invited staff across several divisions to register for voluntary redundancy, with leavers going in the first quarter of 2027, FStech reported on 3 November, citing The Times.
items.why: UK banks are trimming staff as automation spreads, which will shape the business cases banks expect for AI.

items.headline: Monzo weighs new funding at a GBP 7.5 billion valuation
items.summary: Monzo is weighing a new funding round at a GBP 7.5 billion valuation as buyout talks stall, Fintech News Switzerland reported on 6 November, citing the Financial Times.
items.why: Another marker for neobank valuations in a week when Revolut's rose sharply, which keeps pressure on incumbents' digital offers.

items.headline: Revolut valued at USD 115 billion in a secondary share sale
items.summary: Investors including Coatue, T. Rowe Price and Baillie Gifford completed a secondary share sale valuing Revolut at USD 115 billion, 53 percent above a year ago, TechCrunch reported on 4 November. No new money went into the company, which is preparing to launch a US bank.
items.why: Gives Revolut a strong currency for expansion and raises the bar for incumbents' digital offers in Europe.

items.headline: OpenAI's Brockman says enterprise revenue doubled and an IPO could come in 2027
items.summary: OpenAI president Greg Brockman told a Wall Street Journal conference that annualised revenue grew 70 percent in the third quarter as enterprise revenue doubled, and that the company would be ready for an IPO in 2027, TechCrunch reported on 5 November.
items.why: With both leading labs heading for public markets, their pricing and enterprise terms will face investor pressure that banks will feel in contracts.

items.headline: Anthropic's compute took 58 percent of revenue last quarter, up from 48 percent
items.summary: Anthropic's amended filing shows compute taking 58 percent of third-quarter revenue, up from 48 percent the quarter before, TechCrunch reported on 3 November.
items.why: AI pricing for enterprise customers, banks included, depends on whether the labs can bring compute costs down.

items.headline: Anthropic gives Claude Enterprise a security centre and inference hooks
items.summary: Anthropic said on 5 November that a new security centre compares an organisation's settings with its recommended configuration and exports a report for auditors, and that inference hooks are generally available.
items.why: Gives bank security and audit teams evidence they can file, which shortens the path from pilot to approval.
items.for_your_skills: For your skills: Regulatory Audit and Architecture & TOM can cite the exported configuration report and inference hooks as concrete controls.

items.headline: Mistral adds managed agents and workflows to its Studio platform
items.summary: Mistral AI said on 5 November that its Studio platform now lets enterprises build and run agents, workflows and apps.
items.why: Gives European banks that want a non-US model provider another enterprise agent platform to evaluate.

say_it_today: UBS now counts 608 AI use cases in production and the OCC has told its examiners to grade bank AI by its consequences; the useful next figure for any bank is how many of those use cases have a named owner and a tested off switch.
thread: AI moved onto the books this week. UBS, Santander and Intesa counted use cases and euros, Goldman narrowed who may use coding agents, and supervisors in Washington, London and Bern described what they will inspect. The Binance report showed a tampered AI coding tool as the way in. Anthropic's amended filing put compute at 58 percent of last quarter's revenue, up from 48 percent, according to TechCrunch, and US tech stocks fell sharply. The common thread is accountability: for what AI costs, what it earns and who controls it.
